SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8298/38
September 15, 1938
Date

Subject : Hand Grenades Thrown Into The Yong Cheng Tai
Customs Brokerage Hong, House No.10, Lane No.
183, Rue du Consulat.

The Yong Cheng Tai Customs Brokerage Hong (永威泰),
House No.10, Lane No. 183, Rue du Consulat, has been established
at this address for the past five years. Formerly it used to
be located at No.5 Siu Foh Li, Rue Laguerre, and at No.4 Canton
Road. The manager is Hu Tsing Ching (胡晉卿), age 40, native
of Soochow.

Since May, 1938 this shop has transported for its
clients 100 bags of flour to Tientsin. A month ago this shop
received through the post a threatening letter signed Wong Ming
(王明) in which the letter "ordered" the shop to cease trans-
porting flour to North China. Upon receiving this letter, the
shop immediately ceased the transportation of food stuffs. How-
ever, after the anniversary of the outbreak of hostilities in
Shanghai, August 13, 1938, the shop resumed such transportations
and up to the present more than 50,000 bags of flour have been
transported to North China, especially to Tientsin.

At 12.30 p.m. to-day three Chinese called at the shop.
One was dressed in black silk gown, another was wearing a coat
and black hemp trousers, while the third man wore a coat and
blue cloth trousers. The man wearing the black silk gown,
after telling the people in the shop not to move, threw two
hand grenades which he was carrying. One of the grenades
exploded and wounded two shop assistants, namely,

1) Loh Ko Cheng , native of Soochow, age about 40, an
employee of the shop with about 12 years service.
He was wounded in the feet. He was removed to hospital
by the Police.

2) Chen Huan Chang, native of Ningpo, age about 40, an
employee of the shop with about 12 years service. He
was wounded in the head and was removed to Lester

1938年9月15日
日期

事由：向领事馆路183弄10号永成泰报关行投掷手榴弹案。

永成泰报关行（永威泰）位于领事馆路183弄10号，在该地址已营业五年。此前曾设于拉格路（Rue Laguerre）小佛里5号及广东路4号。经理为胡晉卿，40岁，苏州人。

自1938年5月以来，该店为其客户向天津运送了100袋面粉。一个月前，该店通过邮政收到一封署名为王明（Wong Ming）的恐吓信，信中“命令”该店停止向华北运送面粉。收到此信后，该店立即停止了食品运输。然而，在1938年8月13日上海战事爆发周年纪念日之后，该店恢复了此类运输，截至目前，已有超过50,000袋面粉被运往华北，特别是天津。

今天下午12时30分，三名华人来到该店。一人身穿黑色丝绸长袍，另一人身穿外套和黑色麻布裤，第三人则身穿外套和蓝色布裤。身穿黑色丝绸长袍的男子在喝令店内人员不得移动后，投掷了他携带的两枚手榴弹。其中一枚爆炸，炸伤了两名店员，即：

1) 罗科成（Loh Ko Cheng），苏州人，约40岁，该店雇员，服务约12年。脚部受伤。由警方送往医院。

2) 陈焕章（Chen Huan Chang），宁波人，约40岁，该店雇员，服务约12年。头部受伤，被送往莱斯特

（印：副警务总监 1938年9月14日 （刑事））

Japanese Military Guards Remain
At Louza Police Station, Nanking
Road Despite Promise To Leave;
Precautions Claimed As Necessary

US Authorities
Deny Approving
Nippon Actions

Marine Officer Views
Scene Of Bombing
As Observer

JAPANESE CLAIMS
DENIED BY S.M.P.

British Maintain Guard
In Area "Occupied"
By Nipponese

Japanese military gendarmes were still in the compound of the Louza Police Station today despite the promise which Settlement Police authorities claim they received that they would be removed this morning following completion of investigations in connection with the throwing of a bomb at the intersection of Nanking and Kweichow Road at 5:16 p.m. yesterday.

Also remaining at the scene of the bombing today was a detachment of the Seaforth Highlanders, apparently contesting jurisdiction with the Japanese since the incident occurred in the British defense sector. It is believed that they will remain until the Japanese have withdrawn their men from the scene.

The Japanese on their part maintain that they are keeping a small number of men in the compound and at the scene of the incident in agreement with a decision reached by themselves and Settlement authorities. They further speak of their stand having "the full understanding" of Captain M. C. Brown "representing Lieutenant - Colonel H. C. Pierce, commander of the First Battalion of the U. S. Fourth Marines."

Denial Issued

A Marine spokesman today denied that any action taken by the Japanese had the approval of the American authorities or that the Marines were in any way involved in the affair.

At the time of the incident, it was stated this morning, Captain Brown as adjutant of the First Battalion which is doing guard duty at Yu Ya Ching and Subbing Well Roads merely proceeded to the scene of the trouble to see what was going on since the spot was close to the American sector.

When he reached the scene, he was approached by Lieutenant-Colonel Yozo Kikuchi, Japanese gendarmerie commander, who entered into conversation with Captain Brown and informed him that an agreement had been reached with Colonel Charles F. Price, Marine commander, not to extend the Japanese guard into the American sector.

Cards

After a brief conversation, the Japanese officer drew out his card and after signing a "bit of pleasantness" thereon handed it to Brown. The American officer, not having any calling card on him, signed his name on a piece of paper instead.

It now appears that the Japanese in claiming to have "the full understanding" of the American Marines are basing this contention on the slip of paper, which they appear to believe can be taken as proof that Captain Brown approved of the Japanese action.

The Marine authorities state that the incident did not occur in their sector and was not their affair. Captain Brown never entered into any discussion with the Japanese, having been approached by Lieutenant-Colonel Kikuchi who volunteered the information about the incident. He was merely showing natural interest in an incident close to his guard post and had neither the authority nor intention of approving Japanese action.

Japanese Remain

As an aftermath to yesterday's bombing incident on Nanking Road, a small force of Japanese gendarmes was still stationed at the Louza Police Station, in the heart of the "department store district," this morning.

Besides the unit of gendarmes in the compound of the Station, a few sentries were seen near the scene of the bombing.

Special Arrangement

The stationing of gendarmes at the station, Lieutenant-Colonel Yozo Kikuchi, commander of the Japanese Gendarmerie in Shanghai, announced yesterday, was made under a special arrangement with the Shanghai Municipal Police. On Sunday there were 50 men at the station, this number being reduced.

The recurrence of bombing incidents, the Japanese officer said, makes the Japanese authorities "acutely feel the need of taking appropriate measures for self-protection."

Japanese Offer Aid

Immediately after Sunday's bombing, he stated, the Japanese authorities received an offer of assistance from the Shanghai Municipal Police in conducting an investigation.

The proffered aid was accepted, the Japanese claim.

With agreement reached on co-operation between the Japanese authorities and the S.M.P. and measures to prevent the recurrence of incidents, a force of about 50 gendarmes was dispatched to the Louza Station, it is claimed.

Not Interfering

"We have made every effort," Lieutenant-Colonel Kikuchi said, "to emphasize that the Japanese military authorities are eager not to interfere with foreign interests here.

"Our stand appears to have full understanding of Assistant Commissioner G. W. Gilbert, who represented Deputy Commissioner K. M. Bourne, and of Captain M. C. Brown, representing Lieutenant-Colonel H. C. Pierce, commander of the First Battalion of the United States Fourth Marines."

Arrangements for cooperation between the S.M.P. and the Japanese military authorities were discussed at an 1½-hour conference held at the Sun Ya Restaurant, beginning at 9 o'clock last night.

Mainichi's View

Bombing incidents of Saturday and Sunday were caused by an anti-Japanese terrorist band, of between 50 and 60 members, led by Li Chih-min and Yu Tao-san, former Commanders of the so-called "Pootung and Chuansha Guerilla Units", the Shanghai Mainichi claims today.

The terrorist organization, the daily asserts, is maintaining close contact with members of the National Salvation Association and the City Kuomintang.

Jobless Hoodlums

The actual terrorist acts, the journal asserts, are perpetrated by "a handful of jobless hoodlums" and members of the so-called "Fenchien Flying Unit".

"Immediate and resolute" steps must be taken by the Shanghai Municipal Police to put an end to the terrorists' activities, the Mainichi declares. Suitable steps will also be taken by the Japanese authorities, it added.

11 Injured

The grenade, believed to be a military mills type hand grenade, exploded at 5:16 p.m. yesterday on the southeast corner of the intersection as a Japanese naval truck with two marines aboard was proceeding east on Nanking Road, injuring ten Chinese pedestrians and one Sikh policeman. The grenade thrower escaped in the ensuing confusion.

Japanese military and naval officials did not arrive on the scene until an hour and 25 minutes later, but when they did, Japanese sentries were posted on the south side of Nanking Road from Yunnan to Kwangse Roads with fixed bayonets and two military trucks stood by with mounted machine guns. A rigid search of surrounding buildings and civilians was conducted by both police and Japanese authorities, but an unsuccessful one, since no arrest was made in connection with the case.

All but one of the injured persons were discharged from the Lester Chinese hospital last night, and it is expected the eleventh will be permitted to leave shortly. Meanwhile police and Japanese authorities continued their investigations.

尽管承诺撤离，日本宪兵仍驻守南京路老闸捕房；
声称预防措施实属必要

美国当局
否认批准
日本行动

海军陆战队军官
以观察员身份
视察爆炸现场

日本方面声称
遭工部局警务处否认

英军在日本人
“占领”区域维持警戒

尽管租界警务当局声称已获承诺，日本军事宪兵今日仍驻留在老闸捕房大院内。据称，该承诺要求他们在完成对昨日傍晚5时16分在南京路与贵州路路口投掷炸弹一案的调查后，于今晨撤走。

今日留在爆炸现场的还有一支海福尔高地人团（Seaforth Highlanders）的分遣队，由于事件发生在英方防区，他们显然在与日方争夺管辖权。据信，他们将一直停留至日军从现场撤出为止。

日方则坚持认为，根据其与租界当局达成的决定，他们在捕房大院及事件现场保留少量人员。他们进一步声称，其立场得到了“代表美国海军陆战队第四团第一营营长 H. C. Pierce 中校的 M. C. Brown 上尉”的“充分理解”。

发布否认声明

一名海军陆战队发言人今日否认日本采取的任何行动获得了美国当局的批准，也否认海军陆战队以任何方式卷入此事。

据今晨陈述，事发时，担任余姚路和苏宾威尔路（Subbing Well Roads）警卫任务的第一营副官 Brown 上尉，仅因该地点靠近美军区而前往现场查看情况。

当他到达现场时，日本宪兵司令菊池洋三（Yozo Kikuchi）中校上前与他交谈，并告知他已与海军陆战队司令 Charles F. Price 上校达成协议，不将日本警卫扩展至美军区。

名片

简短交谈后，这名日本军官拿出一张名片，在上面签了一句“客套话”后递给了 Brown。由于这位美国军官身上未带名片，他便在一张纸上签下了自己的名字作为替代。

现在看来，日方声称获得美国海军陆战队“充分理解”，是基于这张纸条，他们似乎认为这可以作为 Brown 上尉批准日本行动的证据。

海军陆战队当局表示，事件并未发生在他们的防区内，也与它们无关。Brown 上尉从未与日本人进行任何讨论，是菊池中校主动上前提供了有关事件的信息。他只是对靠近其哨位的事件表现出自然的关注，既无权也无意批准日本的行动。

日军滞留

作为昨日南京路爆炸事件的后续，今晨在“百货公司区”中心的老闸捕房，仍驻扎着一小队日本宪兵。

除了捕房大院内的宪兵部队外，在爆炸现场附近还可见几名哨兵。

特别安排

上海日本宪兵司令菊池洋三中校昨日宣布，在捕房驻扎宪兵是根据与上海公共租界工部局警务处达成的特别安排进行的。周日时有50人在捕房，目前人数已减少。

这位日本军官称，爆炸事件的再次发生使日本当局“深切感到需要采取适当措施进行自我保护”。

日方提供援助

他 stated，在周日爆炸发生后，日本当局立即收到上海公共租界工部局警务处在进行调查方面提供的援助提议。

日方声称，这一提议已被接受。

据称，随着日方与工部局警务处就合作及防止事件重演的措施达成协议，一支约50人的宪兵部队被派往老闸捕房。

不予干涉

菊池中校说：“我们已尽一切努力强调，日本军事当局渴望不干涉在此地的外国利益。

“我们的立场似乎得到了代表副警务总监 K. M. Bourne 的助理警务总监 G. W. Gilbert，以及代表美国海军陆战队第四团第一营营长 H. C. Pierce 中校的 M. C. Brown 上尉的充分理解。”

工部局警务处与日本军事当局之间的合作安排是在昨晚9点开始、历时一个半小时、在新亚大酒店举行的会议上讨论的。

《每日新闻》观点

上海《每日新闻》今日声称，周六和周日的爆炸事件是由一个反日恐怖团伙造成的，该团伙有50至60名成员，由所谓的“浦东和川沙游击队”前指挥官李志民（Li Chih-min）和俞道三（Yu Tao-san）领导。

该报断言，该恐怖组织正与救国会成员及市国民党保持密切联系。

无业流氓

该报刊称，实际的恐怖行为是由“一小撮无业流氓”和所谓的“ fen chien 飞行队”（原文不清，音译）成员实施的。

《每日新闻》宣称，上海公共租界工部局警务处必须采取“立即且坚决”的步骤来终止恐怖分子的活动。该报补充说，日本当局也将采取适当措施。

11人受伤

据信为一枚军用米尔斯型手榴弹于昨日傍晚5时16分在路口东南角爆炸，当时一辆载有两名海军陆战队员的日本海军卡车正沿南京路向东行驶，造成十名中国行人和一名锡克教警察受伤。投掷手榴弹者在随后的混乱中逃脱。

日本军方和海军官员直到一小时二十五分钟后才抵达现场，但当他们到达时，日本哨兵已在南京路南侧从云南路到广西路一带部署，刺刀上膛，两辆装有机关枪的军用卡车在旁待命。警方和日本当局对周围建筑物和平民进行了严格搜查，但未成功，因为此案无人被捕。

除一人外，所有伤者昨晚均已从莱斯特华院出院，预计第十一人也将很快获准离开。与此同时，警方和日本当局继续进行调查。
